value.first: Nights 1-3: when he wakes at 3am, keep it boring and dark. Go in, lay him back down, a few calm words like "night night, still sleeping," and step out within a minute or two. No lifting out of the crib, no lights, no snack, no bringing him to your bed. Expect the first two nights to be his loudest as he tests whether the old routine is coming back.
value.second: Nights 4-7: same script, but stretch your response. Wait 5 minutes before going in the first time, then 10 the next. Keep each visit under a minute and identical. Around now the 3am protest usually gets shorter, even if it doesn't vanish. A rough night in the middle of a good stretch is normal, not a sign it's failing.
value.third: After that: most families see the 3am waking shrink to a brief stir he settles himself within a week or two. If he's overtired going in, try bedtime 20-30 minutes earlier for a few nights, since an 18-month-old who's overtired often wakes harder. If he's still fully waking every night after two weeks, or the waking comes with pain, fever, or trouble breathing, worth raising with your doctor.
